newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Repair craft to be sent to stricken space station.
newsitem.headline: Repair craft to be sent to stricken space station.

text.p: A Russian-American committee of space experts said on Thursday they would send a cargo craft to the stricken Mir orbital station with repair supplies. It was expected to be launched in 11 days' time.
Deputy mission chief Sergei Krikalyov told reporters the 25 to 30 percent loss of electric power caused by Wednesday's accident was an emergency that rated five on a seven-point scale.

"After yesterday's collision we estimated the critical situation on the Mir orbiting station at five on a seven-point scale," Krikalyov said. "Now we must produce the necessary equipment for repairs."
He was speaking after a meeting of a 72-strong expert committee, which included Mir's chief designer and representatives of the U.S. space agency NASA at Korolyov mission control.
In the collision, an unmanned cargo craft bumped into the Spektr module, damaging one of four solar panels and robbing the entire station of up to half its energy supply.

Another cargo craft had been due to leave on a routine supply mission on Friday but has now been postponed by 10 days to gather equipment needed for repairs. The trip from Baikonur launch pad to Mir usually takes two days.
